intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, wandering through the iconic towers and intricate bas-reliefs of Angkor Wat, then continue to the mysterious Bayon temple with its 216 serene stone faces and the jungle-engulfed Ta Prohm temple made famous by Tomb Raider.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Historical Immersion
experiences.description: Gain deep insight into Cambodia's turbulent history by visiting the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 prison) and the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial. Balance the somber experience with a walk through the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda complex to appreciate the country's royal heritage and Buddhist culture.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Spend a day on one of Southeast Asia's most pristine and unspoiled beaches. Swim in crystal-clear turquoise waters, snorkel around coral reefs, and relax on the powder-white sands of Saracen Bay. At night, witness the magical bioluminescent plankton glowing in the water along the shoreline.
experiences.location: Saracen Bay, Koh Rong Samloem Island

experiences.name: Siem Reap Street Food & Cooking Class
experiences.description: Begin with a guided tuk-tuk tour of Siem Reap's vibrant Phsar Leu market to source fresh local ingredients like lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime. Then join a hands-on Khmer cooking class to prepare traditional dishes such as Fish Amok, Lok Lak, and Nom Banh Chok, learning about the rich culinary history of Cambodia.
experiences.location: Phsar Leu Market area, Siem Reap

experiences.name: Battambang Bamboo Train & Wat Banan Temple
experiences.description: Ride the iconic 'Norry' bamboo train — a flat bamboo platform on railway wheels — through the Cambodian countryside past rice paddies and rural villages. Afterward, climb the 358 steps to the hilltop Wat Banan temple, a pre-Angkorian ruin offering panoramic views, and explore nearby bat caves at dusk to watch millions of bats spiral into the sky.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phnom Penh or Siem Reap airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange a budget tuk-tuk or shared taxi transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport convenience store or a late-night street food stall near the resort if available (~$2-4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your airport transfer in advance to avoid overpriced taxis at night. Keep small USD bills handy for tips and tuk-tuks. Cambodia uses both USD and Khmer Riel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely breakfast, take a slow walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to orient yourself. Explore the local beach area, chat with vendors, and soak in the coastal atmosphere of Cambodia's shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest local market or town center by tuk-tuk to pick up essentials, snacks, and get a feel for the local neighborhood. Browse fresh tropical fruits and street snacks. If near Sihanoukville or Kep, explore the waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed sunset on the beach near the resort. Head to a nearby local seafood shack or beachside restaurant for a budget-friendly dinner. Try grilled fish or squid fresh off the boat.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or nearby local café - rice porridge (borbor) with egg (~$1-2 USD)
meals.lunch: Street food from local market - Num Pang (Cambodian sandwich) or fried rice (~$1.50-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Local beachside seafood restaurant - grilled fish with rice and vegetables (~$4-6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally light to allow recovery from travel. Exchange some USD for Riel at a local money changer for small purchases. Tuk-tuks for short distances cost around $1-3 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning beach walk or swim before the heat sets in. Visit a nearby Buddhist temple or pagoda for a cultural experience - most are free or request a small donation. Observe monks during morning alms if timing allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hire a tuk-tuk to explore a nearby historical or cultural site such as a local Khmer village, salt fields (if near Kampot/Kep), or a traditional fishing community. Learn about Cambodian coastal livelihoods from locals.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and explore the local night market if available. Sample Cambodian street food classics like lok lak (stir-fried beef) or amok (fish curry in banana leaf).

meals.breakfast: Local café or resort - French baguette with condensed milk coffee (~$1-2 USD)
meals.lunch: Local Khmer restaurant near the village - rice with fish curry and vegetables (~$2-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Night market street food - various skewers, noodle soups, and fresh spring rolls (~$3-5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting temples - cover shoulders and knees. Remove shoes before entering temple buildings. Bargain politely at markets but do so respectfully.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Kep National Park (if near Kep) or a nearby forested hill area. Hike a beginner-friendly trail through jungle scenery, spot tropical birds, and enjoy panoramic coastal views. Entry fees are minimal (~$1-2 USD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the famous Kep Crab Market (if accessible) or a local fishing pier. Watch fishermen bring in their catch and browse fresh seafood. This is a quintessential Cambodian coastal cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at a clifftop or elevated viewpoint near the coast. Enjoy a budget seafood dinner at a local crab shack - pepper crab with Kampot pepper is a must-try regional specialty.

meals.breakfast: Resort or local stall - rice with fried egg and vegetables (~$1-2 USD)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch with fruits and snacks from the market (~$2-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Local crab market restaurant - Kampot pepper crab with rice (~$5-8 USD, splurge-worthy)

day_by_day.notes: Kampot pepper is one of the world's finest and is grown locally - buy some as a souvenir. Wear comfortable shoes for hiking. Bring water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Phnom Penh via budget bus or shared taxi (~$5-8 USD, 3-4 hours from coastal areas). Book tickets the night before at a local guesthouse or bus station. Enjoy the passing Cambodian countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh and check into a budget guesthouse in the BKK1 or Riverside area (~$8-15 USD per night). Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda - a stunning example of Khmer architecture. Entry fee ~$6.25 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Tonle Sap and Mekong Riverside promenade. Watch the sunset where the rivers meet. Explore the lively Sisowath Quay area with its mix of local and tourist restaurants.

meals.breakfast: On the road - snacks from bus station (~$1-2 USD)
meals.lunch: Roadside stop or local restaurant in Phnom Penh - Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) (~$2-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant - amok fish curry with jasmine rice (~$4-6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Store luggage at your guesthouse before sightseeing. The Royal Palace closes at noon for lunch and reopens at 2pm. Dress code strictly enforced - no shorts or sleeveless tops.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) - a sobering but essential historical site that documents the Khmer Rouge regime. Entry fee ~$3 USD. Allow 2-3 hours. This is deeply moving and historically significant.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial (~$3 USD entry), located about 15km from the city. The audio tour is included and provides powerful historical context. Reflect on Cambodia's tragic recent history.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) for souvenir shopping and local snacks. Enjoy dinner at a local Khmer restaurant away from the tourist strip for better prices. Try beef lok lak or Khmer red curry.

meals.breakfast: Local café near guesthouse - baguette with pâté and iced coffee (~$2-3 USD)
meals.lunch: Simple Khmer eatery near Tuol Sleng - rice with mixed vegetables and tofu (~$2-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Local Khmer restaurant - lok lak beef with rice and egg (~$3-5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Killing Fields and Tuol Sleng are emotionally heavy sites. Take time to process. Photography is permitted but be respectful. Hire a tuk-tuk for the full day (~$10-12 USD) for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Phnom Penh to Siem Reap by budget bus (~$6-9 USD, 5-6 hours). Book with Giant Ibis, Mekong Express, or Virak Buntham for reliability. Enjoy the flat Cambodian plains and rural scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Siem Reap and check into a budget guesthouse near Pub Street or the Old Market area (~$8-15 USD). Freshen up and take a slow walk through the Old Market (Phsar Chas) to browse local crafts, spices, and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pub Street and the surrounding alleys for affordable food options. Visit the famous $1 draft beer strip and enjoy a lively atmosphere. Try Khmer BBQ or a set dinner menu at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: On the bus or at Phnom Penh bus station - baguette or fruit (~$1-2 USD)
meals.lunch: Bus stop roadside restaurant - rice with grilled chicken (~$2-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Pub Street area - Khmer BBQ set with vegetables and dipping sauces (~$4-6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Siem Reap is the gateway to Angkor Wat. Book your Angkor Archaeological Park pass in advance or early morning at the ticket office. 1-day pass: $37 USD, 3-day pass: $62 USD - the 3-day pass is strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn departure (4:30-5am) by tuk-tuk to Angkor Wat to witness the iconic sunrise over the ancient temple reflected in the moat. This is one of the most breathtaking sights in Southeast Asia. Explore Angkor Wat's galleries, bas-reliefs, and towers (~3 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom complex - visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 enigmatic stone faces, the Baphuon, Elephant Terrace, and Terrace of the Leper King. These are extraordinary examples of Khmer Empire architecture and history.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ta Prohm temple (the 'Tomb Raider' temple) where massive tree roots engulf ancient stone structures - best visited in late afternoon light. Return to town for a well-deserved dinner and foot massage (~$5-7 USD for 1 hour).

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks and water from guesthouse - energy bars and fruit (~$1-2 USD)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Angkor complex - rice with Khmer curry (~$3-4 USD)
meals.dinner: Old Market area restaurant - fish amok with rice and fresh lime juice (~$4-6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Start very early to beat the heat and crowds at Angkor Wat sunrise. Bring plenty of water (buy at temple entrance ~$0.50), sunscreen, and a hat. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Hire a knowledgeable tuk-tuk driver for the full day (~$12-15 USD).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the lesser-known but spectacular Banteay Srei temple (~35km from Siem Reap), famous for its intricate pink sandstone carvings considered the finest in Angkor. Also visit Banteay Samré on the return. These are quieter and less crowded than the main complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Cambodian Landmine Museum (entry ~$5 USD) on the return journey - a moving and educational experience about the ongoing landmine crisis in Cambodia and the work of local demining efforts. Return to Siem Reap and visit the Artisans Angkor workshop (free entry) to see traditional Khmer silk weaving and stone carving.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your final evening in Siem Reap at the Night Market. Browse handmade crafts, silk scarves, and Angkor-inspired artwork. Watch a free traditional Apsara dance performance if available at a local restaurant offering cultural shows.

meals.breakfast: Local café - rice porridge with pork and ginger (~$1.50-2 USD)
meals.lunch: Countryside roadside stall near Banteay Srei - grilled corn, spring rolls, noodles (~$2-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Night Market food court - mix of Cambodian dishes from various stalls (~$3-5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei requires your Angkor pass. Negotiate a full-day tuk-tuk rate (~$15-18 USD) for the outer temple circuit. Artisans Angkor products make excellent ethical souvenirs that support local artisans.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cambodia - visit the Siem Reap Provincial Museum (free or minimal entry) for a deeper understanding of Khmer history and artifacts. Alternatively, rent a bicycle (~$2-3 USD/day) and cycle through the peaceful countryside villages surrounding Siem Reap.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Old Market for Cambodian spices, silk, kramas (traditional scarves), and local coffee. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Enjoy a final Khmer meal at a local restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Siem Reap International Airport for your departure flight. Reflect on 10 incredible days exploring Cambodia's beaches, history, and culture. Carry home memories of ancient temples, warm smiles, and unforgettable flavors.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast - num banh chok (Khmer noodles with green curry fish sauce) at a local market stall (~$1-2 USD)
meals.lunch: Old Market food stalls - Cambodian fried noodles (mi cha) with vegetables (~$2-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport or pre-departure meal - keep it light and budget-friendly (~$4-6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2 hours before your flight. Use remaining Riel for snacks as it is difficult to exchange outside Cambodia. A tuk-tuk to Siem Reap airport costs ~$3-5 USD. Total estimated daily budget: $25-45 USD per person including accommodation, food, transport, and entry fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phnom Penh or Siem Reap International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort facilities.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at the resort's 24-hour service or a light room service option upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — arrival is late at night. Confirm your airport transfer in advance. Have local currency (Cambodian Riel or USD) ready for tips and incidentals. Rest well for the full days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort, then take a relaxing stroll along the beachfront to get acquainted with the surroundings. Spend time unwinding by the beach or pool to recover from travel fatigue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest local town or village on foot or by tuk-tuk. Visit a local market to browse fresh produce, handicrafts, and souvenirs. Get a feel for everyday Cambodian life and pick up some essentials.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the beach at the resort's bar, followed by dinner at a beachside restaurant nearby. Enjoy fresh seafood and Khmer cuisine while listening to the sound of the waves.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy tropical fruits, eggs, and local rice porridge (borbor)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local market food stall — try Num Banh Chok (Khmer noodles) for around $2–4
meals.dinner: Beachside seafood restaurant near the resort — grilled fish, amok curry, and jasmine rice for $10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: November is the beginning of the dry season in Cambodia — expect warm, sunny weather with low humidity. Perfect beach conditions. Use sunscreen and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided snorkeling or boat trip to a nearby island or coral reef. Explore the underwater life of the Gulf of Thailand or South China Sea, depending on your resort's coastal location. Depart early morning for the best water clarity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to shore and visit a nearby historical or cultural site — explore a local Buddhist temple (pagoda/wat) in the area. Observe monks, admire traditional Khmer architecture, and learn about local religious practices.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local night market for dinner and cultural immersion. Browse handmade crafts, try street food, and enjoy live traditional Cambodian music if available.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — fresh fruit smoothies, toast, and eggs
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch or buy snacks from the boat tour operator; fresh coconut and tropical fruit on the island
meals.dinner: Night market street food — Lok Lak (stir-fried beef), spring rolls, and fresh sugar cane juice for $5–8 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the snorkeling/boat tour through the resort or a reputable local operator the day before. Bring waterproof sunscreen, a rash guard, and a dry bag for valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Morning kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding along the coastline. Explore hidden coves and mangrove areas at your own pace. Many resorts offer equipment rental at reasonable rates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local fishing village by longtail boat. Interact with local fishermen, learn about traditional fishing techniques, and witness the authentic coastal way of life in Cambodia.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class at a local restaurant or resort — learn to make classic Khmer dishes such as Fish Amok, Green Mango Salad, and Khmer Red Curry. A hands-on cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at resort — rice porridge with ginger and pork, tropical fruit platter
meals.lunch: Lunch at the fishing village — fresh grilled catch of the day with rice for $5–7
meals.dinner: Enjoy the dishes you cooked during the cooking class — typically included in the class fee ($20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes must be booked in advance. Check with the resort's concierge for recommended local operators. Wear comfortable, casual clothing for water activities in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — arrange a transfer from the beach resort to Phnom Penh (Cambodia's capital) by bus, shared taxi, or domestic flight depending on your resort's location. Enjoy the scenic countryside en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh and check into a mid-range guesthouse or hotel in the city center. Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — marvel at the stunning Khmer architecture, the Emerald Buddha, and the royal gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Tonle Sap and Mekong riverfront promenade (Sisowath Quay). Browse riverside bars and restaurants, and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of the capital city at night.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant or rest stop during the journey — try Khmer BBQ skewers and sticky rice for $3–5
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant in Phnom Penh — Amok Trei (fish amok), Beef Lok Lak, and fresh lime soda for $10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: The journey from coastal areas to Phnom Penh can take 3–6 hours by road. Consider a morning departure to maximize afternoon sightseeing. Book city accommodation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply moving and historically significant site documenting the Khmer Rouge era. Allow 2–3 hours for a thorough visit. A sobering but essential part of understanding Cambodian history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial, located about 15 km from the city center. Tour the grounds with an audio guide, visit the memorial stupa, and pay respects at this UNESCO-recognized site of historical importance.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Phnom Penh Night Market (Phsar Reatrey) for shopping and street food. Visit the National Museum of Cambodia if it has evening hours, or enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance at a local cultural center.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery near the hotel — French-influenced baguette sandwiches (a legacy of French colonialism) and iced coffee for $3–5
meals.lunch: Restaurant near Tuol Sleng — try Khmer comfort food like Samlor Korko (vegetable and pork soup) for $5–8
meals.dinner: Traditional Khmer restaurant in the city — set menu with multiple dishes for $12–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy. Take your time and be respectful. Dress modestly and speak quietly. Hiring a local guide ($10–15) adds invaluable personal context to the history.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia — one of Southeast Asia's finest museums, housing an extensive collection of Khmer art, sculptures, and artifacts dating back to the pre-Angkorian era. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco building filled with gold jewelry, clothing, electronics, and local goods. Practice your bargaining skills and pick up unique souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Travel by bus or minivan to Siem Reap (approximately 5–6 hours). Arrive in the evening and check into a mid-range guesthouse near Pub Street or the Old Market area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — Khmer-style rice porridge and iced tea
meals.lunch: Central Market food court — fresh noodle soup (Kuy Teav) and spring rolls for $3–5
meals.dinner: Dinner upon arrival in Siem Reap — try a restaurant on Pub Street for Khmer cuisine; Fish Amok and Beef Lok Lak for $8–12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Phnom Penh to Siem Reap bus ticket in advance through Giant Ibis or Mekong Express for a comfortable and reliable journey. Alternatively, take a 45-minute domestic flight for around $50–80.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise experience. Arrive at Angkor Wat by 5:00–5:30 AM to secure a good spot by the reflecting pool. Watch the sun rise over the world's largest religious monument — a truly unforgettable moment. Explore the main temple complex afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Angkor Archaeological Park — visit the Bayon Temple (famous for its 216 serene stone faces) and Ta Prohm (the 'Tomb Raider' temple, where massive tree roots engulf ancient stone walls). Hire a licensed local guide for deeper historical insight.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap for rest and refresh. Visit the Old Market (Phsar Chas) for souvenir shopping. Enjoy dinner and live traditional music at a cultural restaurant in town.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks and water for the early morning — grab a light bite near the Angkor entrance; local vendors sell baguettes and fruit
meals.lunch: Restaurant near the Angkor complex or a packed lunch — Khmer noodles and coconut water for $5–7
meals.dinner: Siem Reap cultural restaurant — Khmer BBQ or set dinner with Apsara dance performance for $15–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62 USD) to cover multiple days of temple exploration. Wear lightweight, breathable clothing and comfortable walking shoes. Bring a hat, sunscreen, and plenty of water. Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) to respect the sacred sites.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Angkor Thom — the last great capital of the Khmer Empire. Explore the South Gate, Elephant Terrace, Terrace of the Leper King, and Phimeanakas. The scale and detail of the carvings are extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the outer temples of the Angkor complex — visit Banteay Srei (the 'Citadel of Women'), known for its intricate pink sandstone carvings and considered one of the finest examples of Khmer art. Then visit Preah Khan, a sprawling jungle temple with atmospheric corridors.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Apsara dance performance at Angkor Village Theatre or Phare, the Cambodian Circus — a spectacular show blending acrobatics, storytelling, and traditional arts. A unique and uplifting cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café near the hotel — fresh fruit, eggs, and Khmer iced coffee
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant near Banteay Srei — local rice dishes and stir-fries for $5–8
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner at a restaurant near the performance venue — Khmer curry and fresh vegetables for $10–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is about 25 km from Siem Reap — arrange a tuk-tuk or join a guided tour. Book Phare Circus or Apsara performance tickets in advance online. The Phare Circus strongly supports Cambodian youth arts education — a worthy cause.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to a floating village on Tonle Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Take a boat tour through the stilted houses and floating schools, and observe the unique way of life of the lake communities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap for last-minute souvenir shopping at the Artisans Angkor workshop — watch skilled craftspeople create traditional silk, lacquerware, and stone carvings. Purchase ethically made, high-quality Cambodian handicrafts directly supporting local artisans.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Siem Reap International Airport for your departure flight. Reflect on 10 incredible days of history, culture, and beach bliss across Cambodia.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast in Siem Reap — fresh tropical fruit smoothie bowl and toast at a local café
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Old Market — Khmer sandwich (num pang) with pâté and pickled vegetables for $2–3
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an early dinner at a restaurant near Artisans Angkor before heading to the airport

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time and plan your airport transfer accordingly — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure. Keep some USD for any last-minute purchases or airport fees. Ensure you have all receipts for any antiques or art to avoid customs issues.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phnom Penh or Siem Reap International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be arranged to whisk you directly to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a warm welcome with a traditional Khmer greeting, chilled towels, and a complimentary welcome drink at the resort. Check in, unwind, and settle into your beachfront villa.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome snack platter and herbal teas arranged by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Ensure your private airport transfer is pre-booked through the resort concierge. Request a late check-in amenity package in advance. Keep Day 2 light to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start. Take a private sunrise yoga session on your beachfront villa terrace arranged by the resort's wellness team. Follow with a full indulgent breakfast at the resort's signature oceanfront restaurant, savoring fresh tropical fruits, Khmer-style congee, and French pastries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on a private guided snorkeling excursion along the pristine coral reefs just off the resort's beach. A luxury catamaran with a personal guide, snorkeling gear, and chilled refreshments will be at your disposal. Return to the resort for a 90-minute traditional Khmer herbal massage at the resort's spa.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private sunset cocktail experience on the beach — the resort sets up a bespoke bar setup with a mixologist crafting signature Cambodian-inspired cocktails using local ingredients like lemongrass, tamarind, and palm sugar.

meals.breakfast: Oceanfront breakfast buffet at the resort's signature restaurant — tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, Khmer rice porridge (bobor), fresh juices
meals.lunch: Light beach BBQ lunch on the catamaran — grilled prawns, fresh mango salad, coconut rice
meals.dinner: Private candlelit beach dinner at the resort featuring a curated 5-course Khmer tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the snorkeling excursion and spa treatment the night before through the concierge. November weather in Cambodia is typically dry and pleasant — ideal for water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on a private half-day cultural excursion to a nearby traditional Khmer fishing village. Meet local fishermen, learn about traditional net-weaving techniques, and observe the daily rhythms of coastal Cambodian life. A knowledgeable private guide provides historical and cultural context throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby Buddhist temple complex for a guided cultural tour. Light incense, observe monks during afternoon prayers, and learn about Theravada Buddhism's role in Cambodian society. Return to the resort and enjoy leisure time at the infinity pool overlooking the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Apsara dance performance arranged exclusively for resort guests — a classical Khmer art form dating back to the Angkor Empire — held in the resort's open-air pavilion.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — Cambodian banana pancakes, fresh coconut, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a curated local seafood restaurant near the fishing village — steamed whole fish with ginger, stir-fried morning glory, and jasmine rice
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the resort's premium restaurant — pan-seared barramundi, amok curry, and lychee panna cotta for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) when visiting the Buddhist temple. The resort concierge can arrange a sarong if needed. Tip the Apsara performers generously as a cultural courtesy.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early via a private luxury vehicle or chartered speedboat for a day trip to a nearby uninhabited island. Enjoy exclusive access to pristine white-sand beaches with crystal-clear turquoise waters. Bring snorkeling gear, paddleboards, and a fully stocked luxury picnic hamper prepared by the resort's chef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the island — kayak through hidden sea caves, go stand-up paddleboarding, or simply relax under a private cabana set up by resort staff. A personal butler accompanies the excursion to cater to all needs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Enjoy a rejuvenating dip in the resort's private plunge pool before heading to a beachside fire pit gathering with fellow guests or a private romantic setting — roasted marshmallows, storytelling, and stargazing.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast box prepared by the resort — croissants, tropical fruit cups, yogurt parfait, and thermos coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet luxury picnic on the private island — charcuterie boards, lobster rolls, cold-pressed juices, and Cambodian sticky rice desserts
meals.dinner: Sunset dinner at the resort's overwater terrace restaurant — grilled lobster, Khmer green curry, and mango sticky rice

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the private island excursion 48 hours in advance with the concierge. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only to protect the marine ecosystem. Bring a light jacket for the boat ride back in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private charter flight or luxury speedboat transfer to Siem Reap — the gateway to the legendary Angkor Archaeological Park. Check in to a pre-arranged luxury boutique hotel in Siem Reap (coordinate with the Aegean Bliss Resort concierge for seamless arrangements). Begin the afternoon with an orientation walk through the charming French Quarter of Siem Reap.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum for a comprehensive and immersive introduction to the history and civilization of the Khmer Empire. Explore its eight galleries filled with thousands of artifacts, Buddha statues, and multimedia presentations — an essential primer before visiting Angkor Wat.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the vibrant Pub Street and Alley West area of Siem Reap. Browse artisan boutiques and galleries showcasing Cambodian silk, lacquerware, and stone carvings before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — full Khmer and Western spread
meals.lunch: Lunch in Siem Reap at Cuisine Wat Damnak — a celebrated fine-dining restaurant known for its modern Cambodian tasting menus using local seasonal ingredients
meals.dinner: Dinner at Embassy Restaurant or Mahob — upscale Cambodian cuisine in an elegant colonial setting with live traditional music

day_by_day.notes: The transfer from the beach resort to Siem Reap may take several hours depending on the route chosen — plan accordingly. Pre-purchase Angkor Archaeological Park passes (3-day pass recommended) through the resort concierge or online in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for a private sunrise visit to Angkor Wat — the world's largest religious monument and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Arrive before the crowds with a private expert guide and watch the sun rise behind the iconic five towers reflected in the lotus-filled moat. Explore the bas-relief galleries depicting scenes from Hindu mythology and the Khmer Empire's history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the enigmatic Bayon Temple at the heart of Angkor Thom — famous for its 216 serene stone faces. Explore the Elephant Terrace, the Terrace of the Leper King, and the Baphuon Temple. Take a private tuk-tuk tour through the ancient walled city of Angkor Thom.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a special private dinner inside the Angkor complex (arranged through premium tour operators with special permits) — a once-in-a-lifetime candlelit dinner near a floodlit temple with a private chef and Apsara dancers performing.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn breakfast box from the hotel — energy bars, fresh fruit, coffee thermos
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Angkor Café or a curated restaurant near the temple complex — fresh salads, Khmer noodle soup, and tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Exclusive private candlelit dinner near Angkor — 4-course Khmer menu with fine wine pairing and Apsara dance performance

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable, and modest clothing — shoulders and knees must be covered at all temple sites. Start as early as 5:00 AM for the sunrise. Bring insect repellent and a refillable water bottle. The private evening dinner requires advance booking through a licensed premium tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the remote and hauntingly beautiful jungle temple of Ta Prohm — famously left partially unrestored with giant strangler fig trees growing through its walls (known as the 'Tomb Raider Temple'). Visit with a private guide early morning before tour groups arrive. Continue to the pink sandstone Banteay Srei temple, renowned for its exquisite and intricate carvings — considered the 'jewel of Khmer art.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Preah Khan temple complex — a sprawling maze of corridors, courtyards, and galleries dedicated to the father of King Jayavarman VII. Afterward, take a private guided boat tour on the Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake — visiting floating villages and observing the unique amphibious lifestyle of local communities.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap for a traditional Cambodian cooking class at a luxury culinary studio. Learn to prepare amok fish, lok lak beef, and Khmer banana blossom salad under the guidance of a renowned local chef.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the luxury hotel — fresh tropical fruits, Cambodian rice porridge with pork, and freshly brewed Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside restaurant near Tonlé Sap — fresh fish dishes, green mango salad, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class in a beautifully set private dining room

day_by_day.notes: The boat tour on Tonlé Sap offers a powerful perspective on Cambodia's relationship with water and nature. The lake's water levels are highest in November due to the monsoon season — ideal for boat access to floating villages. Book the cooking class in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private charter flight or luxury vehicle transfer to Phnom Penh — Cambodia's dynamic capital city. Check in to a luxury riverside hotel (arranged by the concierge). Begin with a private guided tour of the Royal Palace and the stunning Silver Pagoda — home to a life-sized gold Buddha adorned with 9,584 diamonds and floors covered with 5,000 silver tiles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia — a beautiful terracotta-colored building housing the world's finest collection of Khmer art, including statues from Angkor dating back to the 4th century. Take a leisurely stroll along the scenic Sisowath Quay riverside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Take a private sunset cruise along the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers on a chartered luxury vessel. Sip champagne while watching the golden sun set over the city skyline, the Royal Palace, and the confluence of the two great rivers.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Siem Reap hotel before departure — eggs your way, Cambodian pastries, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Lunch at Malis Restaurant in Phnom Penh — one of Cambodia's most acclaimed fine-dining establishments with a menu celebrating traditional Khmer cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Topaz Restaurant — Phnom Penh's premier French-Cambodian fine-dining institution with an extensive wine cellar and impeccable service

day_by_day.notes: The Royal Palace is closed on certain mornings — confirm visiting hours with your guide in advance. Dress code applies: shoulders and knees must be covered. The sunset cruise should be booked at least 24 hours in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the morning with a somber but essential visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school converted into a detention center by the Khmer Rouge. A private expert guide provides deeply informative and respectful context about Cambodia's tragic recent history. Follow with a visit to the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (The Killing Fields) — a profoundly moving memorial and museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Decompress with a therapeutic afternoon — visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) for luxury souvenir shopping: Cambodian silk scarves, silver jewelry, and artisan crafts. Then enjoy a 2-hour premium spa treatment at the hotel's wellness center — a traditional Khmer massage with aromatic oils.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the trendy BKK1 neighborhood — browse upscale boutiques, art galleries, and design shops. Enjoy cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the city before a final Phnom Penh dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the luxury hotel — full buffet spread with live cooking stations, Khmer and Western options
meals.lunch: Lunch at Romdeng — a celebrated social enterprise restaurant serving traditional Cambodian cuisine in a restored French colonial villa, famous for its tarantula fritters (optional) and Khmer country food
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a private chef's table experience at one of Phnom Penh's finest restaurants — curated 6-course menu with Cambodian wine and spirits pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — allow time for reflection. A private guide is strongly recommended to provide proper historical context. Photography is permitted in some areas but must be done respectfully. The spa treatment should be booked the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely morning in Phnom Penh. Take a private guided walk through the charming riverside area and visit the Wat Phnom temple — the hilltop pagoda that gives the city its name — for a peaceful final cultural experience in Cambodia. Browse last-minute artisan boutiques along Street 240 for silk products, handmade jewelry, and Cambodian artwork.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for checkout. Enjoy a farewell lunch at the hotel's signature restaurant. A private luxury vehicle transfer to the airport is arranged with ample time before departure. Reflect on 10 extraordinary days exploring Cambodia's ancient temples, vibrant culture, pristine beaches, and complex history.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phnom Penh International Airport. The hotel concierge will arrange fast-track airport assistance and a VIP lounge pass for a comfortable pre-flight experience.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the luxury hotel — a leisurely spread of fresh tropical fruits, pastries, Cambodian coffee, and your favorite dishes from the week
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at the hotel's signature restaurant — signature Khmer dishes, fresh seafood, and a celebratory dessert platter
meals.dinner: Airport VIP lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer at least 3 hours before your flight to account for Phnom Penh traffic. Ensure all purchased artisan goods, silk, and souvenirs are properly packed. Check customs regulations regarding antiques — any item over 100 years old requires an export permit from the Ministry of Culture. Keep all hotel receipts for potential VAT refund claims.
